identity.name: KAYNES TECHNOLOGY IND LTD
identity.industry: Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) & Strategic Semiconductor Enablement

summary.oneLiner: Kaynes delivered strong 33% revenue growth and 39.8% EBITDA growth in FY26 despite near-term revenue misses due to geopolitical delays and metering execution lags, but strategically pivoted toward product-driven revenue (30% target) via OSAT, PCB, and smart metering, with order book at INR9,000cr and cash flow normalization expected within 3 quarters.

one-line thesis: Kaynes delivered strong 33% revenue growth and 39.8% EBITDA growth in FY26 despite near-term revenue misses due to geopolitical delays and metering execution lags, but strategically pivoted toward product-driven revenue (30% target) via OSAT, PCB, and smart metering, with order book at INR9,000cr and cash flow normalization expected within 3 quarters.
financial scorecard: revenue: INR3,626cr (+33.2% YoY); EBITDA: INR5,741cr (+39.8% YoY), margin: 15.8%; PAT (reported): INR3,639cr (10% margin); PAT (normalized): N/A (no major one-offs); order book: INR9,000cr+; net debt: INR2,100cr (D/E 0.2), driven by metering receivables, not core EMS
guidance: revenue growth: outgrow market (16-18%) by doubling it; margin: improve via product mix (30% NPD revenue target); order inflow: strong visibility in PCB/OSAT (INR25,000cr next 5 yrs); capex/commissioning: OSAT Unit 2 commercialized Q2FY26, PCB expansion underway, no new capex announced
order book & pipeline: INR9,000cr+; diversified across EV, industrial, aerospace, railway (Kavach), OSAT, PCB; non-cancelable; 5-year visibility in PCB and OSAT
segment / subsidiary detail: EMS: 65% of revenue, working capital days improved to 53 (from 83 in FY24); Metering: INR971cr revenue (24%), INR1,365cr receivables; OSAT: Unit 1 operational, Unit 2 commercialized Q2FY26; PCB: robust 5-year demand pipeline; Railway: Kavach in trial, 20-25% growth expected; Aerospace: new OEM engagements
growth verticals / optionality: OSAT expansion (INR25,000cr 5-yr visibility); PCB capacity scaling; smart metering software/IP monetization; defense/space product development; transition to B2C brand via metering
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin 15.8% (FY26); improving via product mix (NPD target 30% revenue); metering has higher margin than EMS; cost pressures from supply chain mitigated by vertical integration and automation
capex / expansion: No new capex announced; focus on optimizing existing OSAT/PCB capacity; prior capex for OSAT Unit 1 & 2 and PCB expansion completed
capital allocation: Prioritize debt reduction (D/E 0.2); reinvest in NPD, automation, digital infrastructure; no dividend or buyback mentioned; metering receivables securitization (INR40cr done) to improve liquidity
risks & watch-items: Metering working capital cycle (INR1,365cr receivables); customer project delays (geopolitical); execution consistency in scaling; reliance on government tender timelines; margin compression risk if NPD adoption lags
management quality / tone: Confident but cautious; acknowledged guidance misses; committed to execution discipline; emphasized transition from EMS to ESDM/product company; tone shifted from aggressive targets to sustainable, quality-led growth
non-obvious takeaways: Metering business is 60% EMS legacy revenue — the 'new' revenue is only 40%; securitization progress is slow (only INR40cr done) due to installation delays, not bank reluctance; AI integration already live in 2 plants; board added ex-BEL CFO and ISRO expert — signals defense/space push

themes.driver: Defence/aero/space backlog-to-revenue conversion under indigenization mandates.
